drivingQuestion: Is one who delays the additional prayer to the end of its permitted span blameworthy, even though the mishna permits it all day?
outcomeNote: A single amoraic gloss on the mishna's lemma; no objection is raised and no argument is joined in this unit.

segments.he: וְשֶׁל מוּסָפִין כׇּל הַיּוֹם. אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: וְנִקְרָא ״פּוֹשֵׁעַ״.
segments.en: We learned in the mishna: «And the additional prayer» may be recited «all day. Rabbi Yoḥanan said:» Nevertheless, «one» who postpones his prayer excessively «is called negligent.»

moves.summary: The mishna's clause that the additional prayer may be said all day is quoted as the lemma.
moves.about: the mishna's ruling that the additional prayer may be recited all day

moves.summary: R' Yoḥanan adds that one who delays that long is called negligent.
moves.about: the mishna permits reciting the additional prayer all day, but one who delays it that long is nevertheless called negligent
